limits.decidedAccounts: optional per item (absent means []): unique account ids, each one of the payload's accountIds, else the payload is rejected (shape, duplicate, decided_accounts); a pair whose account is listed already has a final stored decision, so the runtime does not score, decide or research it and writes no DEC row for it
limits.blockList: names (companies, people, products) never to mention; each entry is matched as an ASCII-case-insensitive substring of the draft body and why

plaintext.claimedAt: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in Z

reasons.gate_error: candidate scoring or a pair decision failed; the item is retryable in a later run, and a pair whose decision failed has no DEC row

outcome discarded: check codes from draft-checks-v1.json and why_invalid, joined by commas in fixed order

sealed.why: raw text for the sender only: non-empty, at most 400 characters, and passes the same checks as body except link_missing and no_meeting_offer
sealed.body: raw text; passes every draft check against links and fetchedUrls

plaintext.finishedAt: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in Z

rules: A runId is single-use: the runtime writes CLAIM first, conditionally, before any model call or other row; a reused runId is refused (HTTP 409 RUN_EXISTS) and writes nothing.
A run without DONE is ignored (failed, timed out or still running).
A DRAFT row counts only when its DEC row says outcome drafted.

Sealed text fields are raw, unescaped. A consumer that posts through the Slack API escapes them with escape_slack (checks.py, draft-checks-v1.json escapeCases); the copy-to-clipboard path uses the raw text.
